Guideline: Use createSignal for state, createMemo for computed values
Description: SolidJS uses fine-grained reactivity with signals; each signal creates its own dependency tree
Do: Use createSignal() for mutable state and createMemo() for derived computations
Don't: Use React-style useState/useEffect patterns that cause unnecessary re-renders
Code Good:
const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0);
const doubled = createMemo(() => count() * 2);

Guideline: Use JSX with Solid's createRoot for mounting
Description: SolidJS uses a compile-time JSX transform that creates fine-grained DOM updates without virtual DOM diffing
Do: Write components as functions returning JSX; use props via the props parameter destructuring
Don't: Use class-based components or render functions without JSX

Guideline: Use solid-start or @solidjs/router for file-based routing
Description: @solidjs/router provides React Router-like routing with Solid's fine-grained reactivity; solid-start adds SSR capabilities
Do: Define routes in a router component; use <Route> for path matching and <Navigate> for redirects
Don't: Use window.location for navigation instead of the router
Code Good:
<Routes>
  <Route path='/' component={Home} />
  <Route path='/dashboard' component={Dashboard} />
  <Route path='/login' component={Login} />
</Routes>

Guideline: Use createContext for component tree state; stores for global state
Description: Solid provides createContext/useContext for prop drilling avoidance and createStore for complex state trees
Do: Use context for shared UI state (theme, auth); use createStore for nested data structures
Don't: Pass every piece of state through props from root to leaf components

Guideline: Use createResource for reactive data fetching with loading states
Description: createResource returns a read function and loading/error signals; automatically tracks dependencies
Do: Use createResource for API calls; access .loading and .error signals for UI feedback
Don't: Fetch in onMount without tracking loading state in the template

Guideline: Leverage fine-grained reactivity for zero unnecessary updates
Description: SolidJS only updates the exact DOM nodes whose signals change; no virtual DOM diffing overhead
Do: Keep signal scope narrow; create separate signals for independent UI sections
Don't: Wrap everything in a single signal causing full component re-renders on any change

Guideline: Use native HTML elements with Solid's signal bindings for a11y
Description: Solid's fine-grained updates naturally keep aria attributes in sync; use native <button>, <nav>, semantic elements
Do: Bind aria attributes to signals; use role and tabindex where native elements aren't suitable
Don't: Use div/span as interactive elements without keyboard handlers or aria labels
Code Good: {navItems().map(item => ( {item.label} ))}

Guideline: Use CSS modules or Tailwind with Solid's classList binding
Description: Solid supports dynamic class names via the class directive; works seamlessly with Tailwind CSS and CSS modules
Do: Use classList for conditional classes; use CSS custom properties for theming
Don't: Inline styles with JavaScript objects instead of CSS classes
Code Bad:
// Inline styles everywhere

Guideline: Use @solid-primitives/motion or CSS transitions with signals
Description: Solid primitives library provides motion utilities; combine with CSS transitions for smooth animations
Do: Use transition classes toggled by signal changes; use requestAnimationFrame for complex animations
Don't: Manually manipulate DOM styles without using CSS transitions

Guideline: Use createFormAction with solid-start for server validation
Description: Solid-start provides form actions similar to SvelteKit; validate on the server and display errors reactively
Do: Use createSignal for each field; show inline errors bound to validation state
Don't: Validate only on submit without inline feedback
Code Bad:
// No inline validation
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <input value={name()} onInput={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
  <button>Submit</button>
</form>

Guideline: Use solid-meta or document head manipulation for SEO tags
Description: Solid doesn't have a built-in meta tag system; use the solid-meta package or manipulate document.head directly in SSR context
Do: Define meta tags in layout components; use <svelte:head> equivalent via solid-meta
Don't: Hardcode meta tags in each page without inheritance from layouts

Guideline: Use CSS custom properties with a signal-driven theme toggle
Description: Toggle dark mode by updating a root-level signal; use CSS variables for all color values
Do: Store theme in localStorage and sync via a context provider at the app root
Don't: Define separate light/dark components without shared CSS variables

Guideline: Use native with width/height and loading='lazy'
Description: Solid doesn't include a built-in image component; use the native img element with proper attributes for performance
Do: Set explicit width/height to prevent CLS; use loading='lazy' for below-fold images; prefer WebP format
Don't: Load all images eagerly without size constraints causing layout shift

Guideline: Use <A> component for client-side navigation; Link for styled links
Description: @solidjs/router provides <A> and <Link> components that handle SPA transitions without full page reloads
Do: Use <A href='/path'> for internal navigation; use window.location only for external URLs
Don't: Use window.location.href for every navigation causing full page reloads

Guideline: Use ErrorBoundary component for graceful error handling
Description: @solidjs/router provides <ErrorBoundary> to catch rendering errors and show fallback UI without crashing the app
Do: Wrap route components in ErrorBoundary; provide meaningful error messages and recovery options
Don't: Let unhandled errors crash the entire application with a white screen
